predecessors.name: German Africa
predecessors.text: British Cameroons, 89,526 km2: 'Northern Cameroons and Southern Cameroons'

successors.name: Federal Republic of Nigeria
successors.text: the Northern Cameroons, 'two non-contiguous sections' along the Nigerian border that became the Sardauna Province of Northern Nigeria

successors.name: Cameroon
successors.text: the Southern Cameroons, which 'forms part of the Northwest and Southwest regions of Cameroon'

ledger.x: 1916 (20 July): Britain and France divide German Kamerun.
1922: the territory becomes a League of Nations mandate.
1946 (6 December): the mandate becomes a UN trust territory.
1961 (1 June): the Northern Cameroons join Nigeria.
1961 (1 October): the Southern Cameroons join Cameroon.

wars.name: Kamerun campaign
wars.outcome: Allied victory: Kamerun partitioned between Britain and France on 20 July 1916, the British taking the smaller share.

certainty.note: The mandate boundary with French Cameroun is not described on the page; the Northern Cameroons are two non-contiguous strips whose limits follow the Nigerian border.
